chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

A man freed his slave upon his death, and he had no other wealth besides him. He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'The heirs are to be asked for (to pay) two-thirds of his value.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for freeing a slave upon death if the owner has no other wealth?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific legal mechanism for the *mudabbarr* (slave manumitted upon death) when the estate lacks sufficient liquidity, mandating that heirs cover two-thirds of the slave's value to fulfill the manumission contract. This ruling highlights the prioritization of freeing a slave as a binding debt against the deceased's share of the estate, ensuring the slave's freedom is not contingent on the heirs' voluntary generosity but on their legal obligation.
